transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I’ve been having a really hard time lately with tasks that require a lot of mental focus and effort. I find myself constantly avoiding or putting off things like paperwork or long projects because they just feel too exhausting to even start. It's really starting to impact my daily life.

Have these focus and procrastination problems been present since childhood, or did they start more recently during a stressful period or when your mood changed? About how long have they been going on?

These problems actually go all the way back to my childhood, definitely before I was 12 years old. They aren't due to recent stress or mood changes, and they have been consistently happening for at least the last year.
Do these attention problems happen in more than one setting, like both at work or school and at home, and have they caused noticeable problems in those areas?
To be honest, I haven't really thought about whether it happens in multiple different settings. I'm not entirely sure how much it affects me across those different areas.
Can you give me one example of how these attention problems affect you at work or school, and one example of how they affect you at home or in daily responsibilities?

At work, I constantly delay and avoid writing reports or doing projects because they require so much mental focus. At home, I'm always losing important everyday items like my keys, wallet, or the tools I need to get chores done.

Besides procrastinating and losing things, do you also often make careless mistakes, have trouble sustaining attention when reading or listening, seem not to listen when spoken to, fail to finish tasks, have trouble organizing, get easily distracted, or forget daily activities?

No, I don't really experience those other issues. I don't think I make careless mistakes, and I don't really have trouble organizing or getting easily distracted. It's mostly just the avoiding hard tasks and losing my things that I struggle with.
When you were a child, did parents or teachers also notice attention problems like losing things or avoiding schoolwork, or were these mostly things you noticed yourself?

Yes, both my parents and teachers definitely noticed and complained about those struggles when I was a kid. My teachers were always pointing out that I constantly lost my school supplies or homework, and my parents got really frustrated because I did everything I could to avoid doing my homework or any tasks that required focus.

Since ADHD usually involves several different attention symptoms, are there any other long-standing examples you can think of—like often forgetting appointments, not following through on instructions, or seeming not to listen even when you’re trying?

I don't really struggle with those exact things like forgetting appointments or not listening. Instead, my attention issues mostly show up as constantly losing items I need to get things done, and strongly avoiding or delaying any task that requires a lot of sustained mental effort.
Aside from losing things and avoiding tasks that need a lot of mental effort, is there any other long-term attention problem you’ve had repeatedly since childhood, even if it seems minor?

No, I can't really think of any other specific attention-related problems besides those. For as long as I can remember, it's really just been about losing my things and doing everything I can to avoid tasks that require a lot of mental effort.
When you avoid these mentally demanding tasks, is it mainly because you get distracted and can’t stay focused, or because you feel anxious, overwhelmed, or low in motivation?

It is definitely because I get easily distracted and find it incredibly hard to keep my focus, rather than feeling anxious or having low motivation. Whenever I try to force myself to do those tasks, my mind just starts to wander almost immediately.
When you read something long or sit through a lecture or meeting, do you often notice your mind wandering or have trouble staying focused all the way through?

Yes, absolutely, I struggle a lot with staying focused during long readings or meetings because my mind wanders constantly. It is so mentally exhausting that I actively try to avoid or postpone those kinds of activities whenever I possibly can.
